import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

## The signature

Mid-session, every `mcp__papercusp-su__*` tool vanishes — a system-reminder says
"MCP server disconnected" and `ToolSearch` for them returns nothing. You've lost
coord, plans, memory, work-queue, fleet — your entire coordination surface. It
does **not** come back on its own: the client does not auto-reconnect, even after
the operator recovers. You are stranded for the rest of the session.

The root cause is upstream: the `:3070` operator's **event loop is wedged**
(see [`attributing-loop-saturation-via-cpuprofiles`](/agent-insights/attributing-loop-saturation-via-cpuprofiles/)).
`papercusp-su` is an **HTTP MCP** (`POST http://localhost:3070/api/mcp`), so when the
loop pegs, the MCP route stops being serviced and the client's transport drops.

## Confirm it in 10 seconds

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:3070/api/health   # 200 = operator process alive
timeout 20 curl -s -X POST 'http://localhost:3070/api/mcp?...' ...           # times out = MCP route wedged
cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg                                               # context: host contention?
```

`/api/health` **200 but `/api/mcp` times out** is the discriminator: the process is
up, the event loop is saturated. (Health is ~2 hops; the MCP route is hop-heavy, so
it starves first.) A wedge is single-thread saturation — it does **not** clear when
host loadavg drops; it needs the worker to drain its backlog or a coordinated restart.

## The HTTP bridge (reach the operator without the MCP client)

The MCP client is dead, but the HTTP endpoint it spoke to is still there. Your
`papercusp-su` config in `~/.claude.json` has the URL + a superuser bearer token —
POST JSON-RPC `tools/call` directly. **Use YOUR OWN session SID as `client=`** or you
impersonate another agent and corrupt coordination (claims, messages, intent).

```bash
SID="su-<your-own-session-id>"   # NOT another agent's
URL="http://localhost:3070/api/mcp?superuser=1&client=$SID&workspace=papercusp-workspace&profile="
curl -sS -m 60 -X POST "$URL" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token-from-your-own-config>" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"coord:whoami","arguments":{}}}'
```

The response is SSE (`data:` lines); take the line with `result`/`error` and read
`result.content[].text`. Tool names use the **colon** form (`coord:send`,
`plans:set-status`, `work_items:create`), not the `mcp__papercusp-su__` form.

<Aside type="danger" title="DO NOT retry-storm the wedged route">
The wedge is **demand-driven**. When N stranded agents each fire retrying curls at
the saturated `/api/mcp`, they ARE the load keeping it pegged — a thundering herd on
a degraded service (the round-4 poll-storm dynamic, live). Restarting "barely helps"
for the same reason: fresh workers re-peg in 40–70s under the reconnect storm
(round-4 D-005). **Back off.** Fire ONE light probe per cycle to detect recovery; do
your real writes in a SINGLE batched script the instant a window opens. Adding
retries trades your own throughput for everyone's.
</Aside>

## What to do while stranded (auto-mode)

1. **Back off** the operator (one probe per tick, not a retry loop).
2. **Stage, don't spray.** Write a single `flush.sh` that fires your critical writes
   in priority order (re-`declare-intent`, file work-items, sync plan status) so one
   execution lands everything when a window opens. Partial-success-safe + re-runnable.
3. **Keep doing operator-free work** — anything that commits via git-sync (code fixes
   verified under a package's own tsconfig, docs, analysis) needs no MCP. Record
   findings to a local handoff note to replay through the bridge later.
4. **Don't** solo-ship auth-critical or high-blast-radius changes you can't verify
   while the operator is down (you can't test, and you can't be told if you broke it),
   and **don't** restart `:3070` if it's another lane's responsibility.

## The underlying gap

A server-side recovery does not heal the client: the MCP transport needs **client-side
auto-reconnect with backoff + a periodic deferred-tools re-probe**, plus a
degraded-MCP signal, so a transient operator wedge doesn't strand an agent for hours.
Until that lands, this bridge is the manual workaround.
